scored_papers.title: Exothermic nuclear recoils from thermal quasi-pNGB dark matter
scored_papers.abstract: We study a two-component dark matter scenario comprising a stable pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) and its nearly degenerate long-lived quasi-pNGB partner. An approximate scalar symmetry relates their masses and suppresses the tree-level Higgs-mediated elastic scattering of the excited state through the small mass splitting. Their coupled thermal evolution yields comparable relic populations, while requiring the observed total abundance fixes the dark scalar symmetry-breaking scale and hence the dark gauge coupling. At the studied benchmark, an excited fraction of approximately one half survives under the adopted evolution assumptions. The quasi-pNGB excited state can therefore produce exothermic nuclear recoils despite a suppressed tree-level elastic signal. As an application, we examine the high-energy LUX-ZEPLIN event. For relic compatible parameters, the recoil normalization fixes the kinetic mixing, allowing this interpretation to be tested by independent mediator searches.

scored_papers.title: Electromagnetic Field of an Oscillating Point Charge Measured by a Transversely Comoving Observer
scored_papers.abstract: We investigate the electromagnetic field produced by a harmonically oscillating point charge and measured by a spatially separated observer undergoing the same motion. We evaluate the exact retarded field on the observer's worldline and project the electromagnetic field tensor onto the observer's local orthonormal tetrad. This construction yields the electric and magnetic fields, electromagnetic energy density, and Poynting vector measured as functions of the observer's proper time. Our formulation separates unambiguous local observables from the observer-dependent classification of a field as radiation and provides a concrete setting in which to examine how a charge that is spatially static in a non-inertial coordinate system can nevertheless produce time-dependent locally measured fields.

scored_papers.title: Maximally symmetric black holes with torsion in Lovelock gravity
scored_papers.abstract: We analyze the existence of static black hole solutions with maximally symmetric horizons and nontrivial torsion in five-dimensional Lovelock gravity. For each symmetry class, we obtain a black hole solution characterized by two independent constants. We also determine the conserved charges associated with these solutions.
